item.title: Siri AI Is Becoming Apple’s Everything Tool
item.description: Apple’s revamped Siri is more than a voice assistant; it’s now the backbone of the iPhone user experience. You can try it now through the iOS 27 public beta.

item.title: Scientists’ Side Hustle? Using AI and Quantum Computing to Generate New Peptides
item.description: Researchers cobbled together funding and time to show how quantum computing could aid in the development of drugs to help underserved populations and combat rare diseases.

item.title: OpenAI’s Head of Safety Is Leaving the Company
item.description: Johannes Heidecke’s departure comes as OpenAI tries to further integrate its research and safety teams.

item.title: Apple Is Suing OpenAI for Allegedly Stealing Hardware Secrets
item.description: The iPhone maker claims OpenAI encouraged poached employees to bring over confidential presentations, secret prototypes, and key supplier details.

item.title: A New Experiential Gallery Just Might Change Your Mind About AI Art
item.description: Billed as the “world’s first museum of AI arts,” Dataland uses wearables and troves of material from the Amazon to merge nature, biometrics, and art.

item.title: Robot Dogs, Teslas, and Rescue Helicopters: The UN AI Summit Was a Lot
item.description: Amid live coding sessions and Silicon Valley optimism, the UN’s AI for Good summit wrestled with an urgent question: Can global governance catch up before the technology races beyond its control?

item.title: OpenAI’s CEO of AGI Deployment, Fidji Simo, Is Stepping Down
item.description: The move comes after Simo took significant medical leave. She will stay on as a part-time adviser.

item.title: Anthropic Wants You to Pay Up for Claude Fable 5
item.description: Claude subscribers must soon pay usage-based fees to access Anthropic’s best consumer AI model—a sign that the golden era of AI subscriptions is ending.

item.title: The 1X Neo Robot Has Freaky Fast Fingers
item.description: The soft, oddly intimate home-chore robot has been given some very tactile hands.

item.title: The $28 Million Mistake That Inspired Estonia’s AI ‘Fuckup Finder’
item.description: A single wording mistake cost the government millions. Now Estonia is using AI to spot legal errors before they become law—and to automate more of the state.
